title: Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) - Digital Database and Corresponding Interfaces for ReUse of Architectural Components (v0.6.3.0)
description:
The Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) is a prototypical digital component database. It catalogs digital representations of uniquely identifiable architectural components for reuse. Furthermore, it provides corresponding interfaces and tools to leverage them via a backend REST-API, a web-frontend as well as a interface for direct interaction within Rhino Grasshopper.

Changes in v0.6.3.0 (unreleased)

Added

  • Access tokens (decision 8.167): admins create personal access tokens in Settings (30 days, 90 days or one year; shown once, stored only as a hash, at most 10 active), renew and revoke them; admins see and revoke every token on a new admin page. A token reads the catalog only where its scope allows; GET /auth/token-check tests one. The ground for the MCP layer and the Grasshopper device sign-in of this release.
  • Using CSC from Claude (decision 8.168): an MCP endpoint at https://<api host>/mcp with nine read-only tools (search, components, versions, evidence, datasets, timeline, similar components). Add it as a custom connector in Claude; a browser window opens the consent page on the website, where an admin allows read access to the catalog as they see it in the web app. The connection renews itself for up to 90 days and can be revoked in the token list. Answers carry no e-mail addresses and mark everything that is not public.
  • Grasshopper signs in without a password (decision 8.168): the Session component has a SignIn button (Windows). It opens the browser, you allow "Grasshopper on this computer" on the website, and the sign-in is stored for your Windows user (encrypted with DPAPI, one per server), outside every Grasshopper file. Later runs sign in by themselves and renew their token; SignOut ends the sign-in on the computer and the server. Each sign-in appears in the token list in Settings, where it can be revoked.

Changed

  • Session component: new inputs SignIn and SignOut; Refresh is gone, because the sign-in renews itself. Connected Username and Password still win and stay the way to sign in on macOS; with them the component signs in again by itself when its 6-hour token runs out. Update the components with CSC_Update.
  • Viewer: a "Piece opacity" slider in the Overlay panel fades the mesh, proxy or point cloud so reinforcement and other overlays show through. The Mesh and Point cloud switches are labelled and have an "Off" choice instead of the "Show mesh" and "Show point cloud" checkboxes; "Show edges" moved to the overlays.

Security

  • A password change or reset ends every access token of the account: personal access tokens, Claude connections and Grasshopper sign-ins. Afterwards create a new token, allow Claude again and press SignIn again.

Server notes

  • CSC_PAT_ROLES (optional, default admin) names the roles that may create access tokens.
  • The new collections access_tokens, oauth_clients, oauth_requests, oauth_codes and oauth_used_refresh need the same database rights as the others; their indexes are created at the start.
  • Set CSC_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://<api host> (no path) in the backend environment: it turns on /mcp and the OAuth server and is the address the connector is given. It also becomes the base of the links in the JSON-LD export (if it was unset so far, those links took the request's own address). After the restart, check that https://<api host>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp answers, then add the connector once in claude.ai.
  • The deploy installs the MCP Python SDK (mcp) and its dependencies (cryptography among them).
  • In read-only mode /mcp and the token renewal keep working; a code issued just before the switch can still be exchanged once. New consents are refused until the flag is gone.

Full history: CHANGELOG.md
